dialogueBeats.shotDescription: Rain starting properly now. Two hundred blue shipping containers, stacked three high, stencilled HANDS OF THE GULF - MEDICAL SUPPLIES - DO NOT DELAY. A watchman's radio playing salsa in an empty office. Gulls asleep on the light standards.

EDDIE MARIN, 40s, dock foreman, walks the rows with a flashlight and a clipboard in a plastic sleeve. He is counting. He gets to the end of a row, looks at the number, and goes back to the start of the same row.
He counts it again. It does not come out the same.
He stops at crate nineteen. He knocks on it with his knuckles. It does not sound like bandages. It sounds like something packed tight and heavy and wrapped in plastic.
He knocks again. From inside, faintly - nothing.
He writes something down. The pencil breaks. He looks at the broken point for a long moment, then puts the pencil in his breast pocket very carefully, like a man filing evidence.
